classification.difficultyReason: Translate a sum and a weighted difference into two equations, then solve by elimination.

content.prompt:
Solve this problem by introducing two pronumerals and forming two simultaneous equations, even though it can be done more easily using one pronumeral.

The sum of two numbers is 19. Three times one number minus twice the other number is 2. Find the two numbers.

answer.worked:
Let $x$ be the number multiplied by 3 and $y$ the other number.

$$\begin{align*}x+y&=19 &&(1)\\3x-2y&=2 &&(2)\end{align*}$$

Multiply equation (1) by 2, then add equation (2):

$$\begin{align*}2x+2y&=38\\(3x-2y)+(2x+2y)&=2+38\\5x&=40\\x&=8\end{align*}$$

Substitute $x=8$ into equation (1):

$$\begin{align*}8+y&=19\\y&=11\end{align*}$$

The two numbers are $8$ and $11$.

Check: $8+11=19$ and $3\times8-2\times11=2$.
